title: Random forest on aptamer proteomics proposes a protein signature for Parkinson's disease
summary: Proteins measured with the SomaLogic aptamer platform in 1599 serum, 85 cerebrospinal fluid and 37 brain tissue samples were analysed with random forest machine learning to derive multi-protein signatures. The most consistent classifier gave AUCs of 0.74 in cerebrospinal fluid, 0.75 in brain and 0.66 in serum, and 0.72 in serum for severe disease versus controls. The classifiers were significantly related to disease status in a validation data set (P < 0.001). The AUCs are modest and the authors describe the signature as deserving further biomarker evaluation.
ai_technology: Random forest on SomaLogic aptamer proteomic data

evidence.tested: Cross-modality replication and a separate validation data set for the classifier signatures.
evidence.unknown: Clinical utility, specificity versus other diseases and the number of validation samples; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest models derived multi-protein disease signatures.
